data.body:
Closes: 8 of 15 children now closed. Closed this round after verifying ACs against the merged tree (59 tests green on gerrit/main, plus the cli-reference, MCP-model-drift and types-drift gates all clean there): 91b0 F8, bc66, 0af1 F14, 70f5 F9, a516 F6, 6850 F2, 62eb F5, cacb F4. bc66 closing reported unblocked: 1daf, so F11 is genuinely unblocked by the edge.

TWO CLOSES REFUSED, correctly, and I did not force them.

ce8f (F7) and e755 (F3) were refused because their merged commits touch src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py — and for ce8f also src/rebar/types.py — which their recorded file_impact never declared. The gate is right: that work DID go beyond the reviewed plan. It was added later, by the subagent fixing the public-types drift gate, once we learned types.py is GENERATED and hand-added constants vanish on regeneration. The reviewed plans predate that discovery and describe only the consuming modules.

The gate names two paths: declare the files (a MATERIAL plan change that invalidates the attestation and requires a fresh review-plan), or --force. Agents must not use force overrides, and this is exactly the case the prohibition is for — forcing would close a ticket whose recorded plan does not describe what actually shipped, leaving no durable record that the generator seam was part of this work.

So I widened file_impact on both to declare gen_types.py (and types.py for ce8f) with reasons naming why the generator must emit the constant, and re-ran review-plan on both. They close once those return PASS+signed.
